[PATH:empirical] Randomized controlled trial comparing intermittent fasting (e.g., 5:2 or time-restricted eating) with high-protein (≥1.6 g/kg/day) versus standard protein intake over 18-24 months, measuring changes in resting metabolic rate, fat-free mass, and weight loss trajectory. — Directly tests whether high-protein intake attenuates metabolic adaptation in a long-term real-world setting, addressing the core causal claim with controlled conditions.

[PATH:literature] Meta-analysis of existing studies on protein intake and metabolic adaptation during caloric restriction, focusing on subgroups practicing intermittent fasting for >12 months. — Synthesizes available evidence to detect consistent attenuation effects, accounting for heterogeneity in fasting protocols and adherence, and can clarify if the hypothesized effect is supported across populations.

scope.domain: long-term intervention (>12 months), real-world adherence, protein intake ≥1.6 g/kg/day

qualifier.tension: High-protein diets may preserve lean mass and resting metabolic rate, counteracting the metabolic slowdown observed in standard intermittent fasting protocols

C006.subject: Intermittent fasting
C006.object: long-term weight loss efficacy and metabolic health beyond 12 months
evidence_refs: [Simulated evidence for: Intermittent fasting long-term weight loss efficacy and metabolic health beyond 12 months]

[PATH:literature] A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials comparing intermittent fasting (e.g., alternate-day fasting, time-restricted eating) to continuous caloric restriction with follow-up of at least 12 months, focusing on weight maintenance and metabolic markers (e.g., HbA1c, lipids, insulin sensitivity). — Provides pooled effect estimates from existing long-term trials, directly addressing the hypothesis's temporal scope and disputed status by quantifying efficacy and adherence beyond 12 months.

[PATH:empirical] A prospective cohort study in real-world settings (e.g., using mobile health apps or dietary logs) tracking adherence and weight outcomes over 12–24 months in individuals self-selecting intermittent fasting versus standard dietary approaches, with controls for baseline metabolic health. — Captures real-world adherence and long-term metabolic effects outside controlled trial conditions, addressing the scope domain and clarifying whether benefits persist under typical lifestyle constraints.

[PATH:theoretical] A theoretical modeling study incorporating dynamic energy balance and metabolic adaptation (e.g., using differential equations of fat oxidation, hunger signaling, and circadian rhythms) to simulate long-term weight loss trajectories under intermittent fasting versus daily restriction. — Tests mechanistic plausibility of sustained metabolic improvements beyond 12 months, informing whether observed effects are likely due to energy restriction alone or unique fasting-induced pathways, thereby guiding empirical hypothesis refinement.
